hypotheses.justification: Nothing in the statement needs `[W.IsElliptic]` to elaborate. In Mathlib's `Affine/Point.lean`, the group structure on `W.toAffine.Point` (`Add`, then `AddCommGroup` at line 805) sits in a section that only assumes `[DecidableEq F]`. The `IsElliptic` section, lines 540–601, is closed before that and only covers `Point.mk` and `pointEquiv`. So `addOrderOf Q` elaborates without the instance. `IsTwoKernel` is a structure on any `WeierstrassCurve T` with `[CommRing T]`, and `coordsOrZero` only needs `[CommRing R]`; neither mentions `IsElliptic`. The proof never uses the instance either. The first two goals are pure polynomial facts. The third goal uses `addOrderOf_zero`, `addOrderOf_nsmul_eq_zero` and a case split on `Q`. In the `some` case it applies `WeierstrassCurve.eval_Psi2Sq_of_two_nsmul_eq_zero`, which only takes `[Field F] [DecidableEq F]`, a curve `W`, `h : W.Nonsingular x y` and `h2`, and has no `IsElliptic` argument. So the same proof goes through unchanged once the binder is removed. The zero-point case is ruled out by `hQ`, not by the instance.
